To find the maximizer of the likelihood function,
we solve $\Lik'(\th) = 0$ for $\theta$.
For mutually independent data, @eq-Lik gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Lik'(\th)
&= \deriv{\th} \Lik(\th)\\
&= \deriv{\th} \prod_{i=1}^n \p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-deriv-Lik}

@eq-deriv-Lik is the derivative of a product of $n$ factors,
which takes $n - 1$ applications of the
[product rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/math-prereqs.html#thm-product-rule)
and produces $n$ terms.
The log-likelihood avoids this work.
